candidates.title: Localization content and runtime family
candidates.objective: Define engine-light localized-message identity, locale fallback, formatting inputs, content validation, and a thin Unity Localization adapter without coupling domain code to one renderer or engine.
source_requirements: Unicode locale, CLDR, ICU or MessageFormat standards and compatibility boundaries
Official Unity Localization documentation plus shipped-engine localization guidance
Plural, gender, fallback, bidirectional-text, font, accessibility, and content-pipeline evidence boundaries
candidates.exact_next_action: Run the positive-source gate and decide whether message identity, locale fallback, formatting, and renderer boundaries are stable enough to admit a Core and Unity blueprint.

candidates.title: Audio events, mix state, and spatial attachment family
candidates.objective: Define engine-light audio event identity, bus and snapshot state, parameter contracts, and spatial attachment intents with a thin Unity AudioMixer adapter, so gameplay and XR systems raise typed audio intents without coupling to a middleware or a scene singleton.
source_requirements: Official Unity Audio, AudioMixer, and spatializer documentation plus OpenXR or platform spatial-audio guidance
Independent professional middleware documentation (FMOD Studio, Audiokinetic Wwise) and Unreal Engine sound and MetaSounds documentation as second-engine evidence
Accessibility, loudness, and comfort evidence boundaries for headset audio
candidates.exact_next_action: Run the cross-project admission gate and the positive-source gate after Localization moves out of staging; decide whether event identity, mix state, and spatial attachment are stable enough to admit a Core and Unity blueprint.

candidates.title: Locomotion modes, comfort policy, and locomotion intent family
candidates.objective: Define engine-light locomotion mode identity (teleport, snap turn, smooth turn, continuous move), a closed typed comfort policy (vignette, turn mode, turn increment, movement speed, posture), and locomotion intents applied to an immutable state with deterministic replay, with a thin Unity XR Interaction Toolkit locomotion-provider adapter, so gameplay and XR systems raise typed locomotion intents without coupling to a rig, an input reader, or a scene singleton.
source_requirements: Official XR Interaction Toolkit locomotion documentation (locomotion mediator and body transformer, teleportation, snap turn, continuous turn, continuous move, tunneling vignette) at the version pinned by the compatibility profiles
Public platform comfort and locomotion guidance from Meta, PICO, and Apple as first-party evidence that the mode set and comfort options recur across headset platforms

Maintained open-source locomotion implementations (a second-engine XR toolkit and an independent Unity teleport locomotor) with license, maintenance state, and an immutable review ref confirmed by a person
Motion-sickness, comfort, latency, and device-behaviour evidence boundaries that route every such claim to a Device Lab receipt
candidates.exact_next_action: A person confirms the URLs, page paths, version pins, and open-source maintenance state in docs/standards/locomotion/source-manifest.json; then run the cross-project admission gate on docs/standards/locomotion/admission.draft.json and decide whether mode identity, comfort policy, and intent state are stable enough to admit a Core and Unity blueprint.

candidates.title: Scene set identity, transition state machine, and scene-flow intent family
candidates.objective: Define engine-light scene set and scene identity, a declared scene graph with one active scene per set, load, unload, and switch intents applied to an immutable flow state through a transition state machine with typed fade and hold durations, recovery to a declared fallback set, and deterministic replay, with a thin Unity additive scene-loading adapter, so gameplay and XR systems request scene changes as typed intents without coupling to scene names, a loader singleton, or objects that survive loads by discovery.
source_requirements: Official Unity scene-management documentation (SceneManager, LoadSceneAsync, allowSceneActivation, UnloadSceneAsync, SetActiveScene, multi-scene editing, the build scene list) at the version pinned by the compatibility profiles, with Addressables scene loading admitted only as an optional sibling adapter
Public platform guidance on loading, transitions, and comfort during scene changes from Meta, PICO, and Apple as first-party evidence that fade, hold, and recovery recur across headset platforms

Maintained open-source scene-flow implementations (an engine-published open project and an independent scene-reference utility) with license, maintenance state, and an immutable review ref confirmed by a person
Load-time, hitching, and comfort evidence boundaries that route every such claim to a Device Lab receipt
candidates.exact_next_action: A person confirms the URLs, page paths, version pins, and open-source maintenance state in docs/standards/scene-flow/source-manifest.json; then run the cross-project admission gate on docs/standards/scene-flow/admission.draft.json and decide whether set identity, the transition machine, and recovery are stable enough to admit a Core and Unity blueprint.

candidates.title: XR UI shell: panels, wrist and hand menus, pointer and gaze routing, and the shared skin contract
candidates.objective: Define a renderer-neutral, engine-light shell model (panel, wrist-menu, and hand-menu identity; world, head-locked, wrist, and hand anchor kinds; open, close, focus, dock, and follow intents on an immutable state with deterministic replay), typed pointer and gaze routing from named input sources that resolves to exactly one panel, and a skin contract mapping the shared design-language tokens to a closed slot set, with UGUI and UI Toolkit as sibling adapters that each expose one injectable skin seam with a default skin, so every UI-bearing family composes on one shell instead of re-deriving spatial UI, and the Inventory presentation adapters become one client of it without transferring any Inventory evidence.
source_requirements: Official engine world-space UI and XR UI documentation (UGUI world-space canvas and XR UI input, UI Toolkit world-space support, XR Interaction Toolkit UI, gaze, and hand interaction) at the version pinned by the compatibility profiles

Public platform spatial-UI guidance from Apple (windows and ornaments), Meta (spatial UI and hand menus), and PICO as first-party evidence that panels, wrist and hand menus, and pointer and gaze routing recur across headset platforms
Maintained open-source XR UI implementations (a mixed-reality toolkit and a second-engine XR toolkit) with license, maintenance state, and an immutable review ref confirmed by a person

Legibility, comfort, reach, and hand-tracking evidence boundaries that route every such claim to a Device Lab receipt, and the rule that automated or device evidence never transfers between the two renderer adapters
candidates.exact_next_action: A person confirms the URLs, page paths, and version pins in docs/standards/xr-ui-shell/source-manifest.json and admission.draft.json; then run the cross-project admission gate on the draft and decide whether the shell model, routing, and skin contract are stable enough to admit a Core blueprint and two sibling adapter blueprints.

candidates.title: Live tuning: in-headset tuning of design tokens and skin values with export back to the assets that own them
candidates.objective: Define an engine-light tuning model (a closed tunable kind set of float, int, bool, enum, colour, vector2, and vector3; an immutable registry populated by explicit registration; set, reset, reset-all, snapshot, apply, and export intents on an immutable state with deterministic replay; and a bridge to and from the design-language token JSON) and a Unity adapter (explicit binding records to skin assets, live apply through the existing skin seams with diagnostics, an injectable export sink whose device JSON and Editor asset writers let a Play-mode or on-device change survive, and a tuning panel that is one client of the XR UI shell with a UGUI fallback), so a developer wearing the headset changes a colour, size, corner radius, or spacing and sees the effect immediately, and the change lands in the asset that owns it instead of in a rebuild loop; the family proves the plumbing, and whether a value looks right on a device stays a Device Lab receipt.
source_requirements: Official engine documentation for runtime-editable serialized values, ScriptableObject assets, Play-mode change loss, and the Editor asset-writing APIs at the version pinned by the compatibility profiles

Maintained public runtime tuning implementations (an immediate-mode tweak panel and a runtime inspector with one typed drawer per kind) with license, maintenance state, and an immutable review ref confirmed by a person

The repository's own design-language token standard, skin seams, Settings contract, and XR UI shell contract as the seams the family composes on, with the rule that it introduces no second token vocabulary
Evidence boundaries that route every legibility, colour, size, and comfort judgement to a Device Lab receipt, so no package claim says a tuned value is correct on a headset
candidates.exact_next_action: A person confirms the URLs, page paths, and version pins in docs/standards/live-tuning/source-manifest.json and admission.draft.json; then run the cross-project admission gate on the draft and decide whether the tuning model, the binding and export seams, and the panel-as-shell-client rule are stable enough to admit a Core blueprint and one Unity adapter blueprint.

candidates.title: Haptics: per-event, per-controller haptic feedback bound to interaction and audio intents
candidates.objective: Define engine-light haptic event and profile identity, a closed haptic-kind set (transient, continuous, envelope) with amplitude, duration, and optional frequency guard rails, per-controller and per-hand profiles over a closed target set, play, stop, stop-all, and set-profile intents on an immutable last-one-wins state with deterministic replay, and a binding table from the Interaction family's semantic intents and the Audio family's event ids to haptic events, with a thin Unity adapter over XR Interaction Toolkit haptic impulse channels and OpenXR haptic actions, so a grab or a hit fires haptics, audio, and a future feedback effect from one source intent without any of those families depending on this one; the family proves the plumbing, and whether a pattern is felt as intended stays a Device Lab receipt.
source_requirements: Official XR Interaction Toolkit haptic impulse and haptic-feedback documentation, the OpenXR core specification's haptic output (xrApplyHapticFeedback, XrHapticVibration), and the XR_FB_haptic_amplitude_envelope and XR_FB_haptic_pcm vendor extensions, at the versions pinned by the compatibility profiles

First-party Meta Horizon OS and PICO haptics guidance, including Meta's Haptics SDK and Haptics Studio as evidence that authored haptic clips recur, plus Apple visionOS/iOS Human Interface Guidelines on playing haptics and semantic patterns

Unity Input System haptics (IDualMotorRumble, XRControllerWithRumble) and one or two maintained open-source haptics implementations with license, maintenance state, and an immutable review ref confirmed by a person
Felt-intensity, comfort, fatigue, and pattern-legibility evidence boundaries that route every such claim to a Device Lab receipt, so no package claim says a controller vibrated
candidates.exact_next_action: A person confirms the URLs, page paths, section anchors, version pins, and open-source maintenance state in docs/standards/haptics/source-manifest.json and admission.draft.json; then run the cross-project admission gate on the draft and decide whether haptic identity, the kind and profile model, and the binding table to Interaction and Audio are stable enough to admit a Core blueprint and one Unity adapter blueprint.
